programme: RERE, MYCN and TFAP2C converge on the retinoic-acid (RA) signalling circuit itself: RERE's target set includes RARB (the RA receptor), and both MYCN and TFAP2C target CRABP2 (the intracellular RA carrier that delivers ligand to RAR). HOXB13 and HOXB7 are the classic RA-responsive HOX-cluster effectors of that circuit, and ID4, a dominant-negative bHLH, is the differentiation brake RA signalling normally releases. Together this is a differentiation-control programme built around RA-receptor/RA-carrier regulation feeding into HOX-driven and ID-gated differentiation, not a single physical complex.
role_in_a: In colorectal cancer, silencing or dysregulation of this RA/HOX axis is a documented route to dedifferentiation and growth: HOXB13 dysregulation is tied to a WNT:retinoic-acid imbalance (PMID 42184974), HOXB7 drives migration/invasion (PMID 38230780), MYCN acts through a PLK1-linked transcriptional programme (PMID 42205755), and ID-family proteins including ID4 are altered in tumour tissue (PMID 39001993) — each independently placed in CRC, consistent with loss of RA-driven differentiation control permitting proliferation.
role_in_b: In stroke, evidence for this same circuit is much thinner and more indirect: TFAP2C sits in a selenium-driven transcriptional programme that blocks ferroptosis and is protective in an ischemic stroke model (PMID 31056284), and RERE loss-of-function causes a developmental syndrome with brain/craniofacial features that overlap conditions associated with cerebrovascular anomaly (PMID 27087320) — a germline neurodevelopmental phenotype, not adult ischemic pathophysiology. HOXB13, HOXB7, MYCN and ID4 have no retrieved stroke-side evidence at all.
shared_axis: A retinoic-acid-tuned differentiation/stress-response module (RARB–CRABP2, gated by RERE/MYCN/TFAP2C, executed through HOXB13/HOXB7/ID4) could plausibly be co-opted in two directions: loss of its restraint permits colon epithelial dedifferentiation and growth, while its RA/ferroptosis-protective arm (via TFAP2C) limits neurovascular injury after ischemia — but nothing in the record shows the same instance of this circuit operating in both tissues at once.
reasoning: The module is nameable from the network data itself (shared RARB/CRABP2 targeting) and four of six carrying factors are independently and directly placed in colorectal cancer, but the disease-B side rests on a single ferroptosis paper and one developmental-syndrome paper rather than stroke literature proper, and no source treats CRC and stroke together through this axis — hence unexpected rather than established/supported, and moderate rather than strong.
support: PMID 42184974 (HOXB13, WNT:retinoic-acid imbalance dysregulating HOX expression in CRC); PMID 38230780 (HOXB7 mediates colorectal cancer cell migration/invasion); PMID 42205755 (MYCN-associated transcriptional regulation in colorectal cancer via PLK1); PMID 39001993 (ID family protein expression, including ID4, assessed in colorectal cancer); PMID 31056284 (TFAP2C-linked transcriptional programme blocks ferroptosis and treats stroke in a model); PMID 27087320 (RERE de novo mutations cause a developmental syndrome overlapping brain-relevant features).
how_to_falsify: Check whether RERE ChIP or knockdown data actually move RARB expression, and whether MYCN/TFAP2C knockdown/ChIP data move CRABP2, in matched colorectal-tumour and post-ischemic blood/vascular samples; if RARB and CRABP2 expression do not track with these factors in either tissue's patient-group data used to build this network, the proposed RA-circuit link is not real and the account fails.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (stroke) vs colorectal (CRC) — the stroke arm is a peripheral-blood network, not brain or vessel wall tissue, so 'neurovascular protection' is inferred, not directly observed. Only 4 independent cohort pairs underlie the 57 patient-group comparisons, so high recurrence fractions (e.g. ZNF24 at 41/57) may reflect within-cohort correlation rather than independent replication. ZNF24 is the numerically strongest concordant factor here but is deliberately excluded from this account: its targets (VEGFA, PDGFRB, CTNNB1, CCND1, MSLN) and its 'stroke' citation (a circRNA/angiogenesis paper that only mentions it) give no anchor into the RA/HOX programme. DMTF1, FOSL1, FOXP4, ZNF135 and THAP1 also passed the concordance filter but are omitted for the same reason — no RA-pathway anchor and, for THAP1, the retrieved 'stroke' papers are actually about dystonia, not stroke. ID2, the classical MYCN partner in the ID-MYCN axis, is in the single-view exclusion list and was correctly not substituted for ID4. Tissue-generic exclusions (FOS, JUNB, BCL3, VDR, etc.) remove likely confounding AP-1/immune signal, which is why FOSL1, despite surviving concordance, was not folded into the core account.
